target: full repo bug/security/edge-case audit, focused on Astro frontend and Cloudflare Pages contact function

findings.description: The contact endpoint parses request.formData() before any Content-Length/body-size guard and only checks name/email/message presence plus message minimum length. Client maxlength attributes are bypassable, so an attacker can send oversized multipart fields through Turnstile verification and onward to Web3Forms.

Siteverify response validation checks only success === true. The forms set data-action="turnstile-spin-v1", but the server does not validate returned action or hostname, reducing defense in depth if a widget key is reused, mis-scoped, or later broadened.

All six contact scripts re-enable the submit button after a failed API response but do not reset the Turnstile widget. Since Turnstile tokens are single-use and expire after 300 seconds, retries can keep resubmitting the same expired or already-redeemed token until reload.

All six contact forms simulate success whenever no Turnstile widget is rendered. If PUBLIC_TURNSTILE_SITEKEY is missing in a production build, visitors see a success state but no request reaches /api/contact and no email is sent.

The server-only Web3Forms access key is named PUBLIC_WEB3FORMS_KEY and typed as ImportMetaEnv. No current client reference was found, but Astro PUBLIC_ variables are intended for client exposure, so this naming/type contract invites accidental leakage of the key the backend is specifically trying to keep server-side.
